problems.title: Extract a perfect square
problems.question: Simplify √96/8.
problems.idea: Use the stated identity or geometric relation, preserving all domain and endpoint conditions.
steps: √96=4√6, so dividing by 8 gives √6/2.
problems.note: The archive folder is Quiz 08 - Makeup; the printed paper is the Quiz 2 makeup, dated 24 January 2023. Existing folder numbering is preserved.

problems.title: A sign quotient
problems.question: Solve |x|/x<1.
problems.idea: Use the stated identity or geometric relation, preserving all domain and endpoint conditions.
formulas: Domain x≠0; the quotient is 1 for x>0 and −1 for x<0.
steps: Only the negative-input case is strictly below 1.

problems.title: Domain of a radical involving absolute value
problems.question: Find the real domain of y=√(x−|x|).
problems.idea: Use the stated identity or geometric relation, preserving all domain and endpoint conditions.
formulas: Require $x-|x|\ge0$.
steps: For x≥0 the radicand is zero, allowed. For x<0 it is 2x<0, forbidden.

problems.title: A perpendicular to a diameter
problems.question: A perpendicular from a point on a circle to a diameter cuts off a diameter piece equal to half the perpendicular length. Find the ratio of the diameter pieces.
problems.idea: Use the stated identity or geometric relation, preserving all domain and endpoint conditions.
formulas: The point and diameter endpoints form a right triangle; its altitude satisfies $h^2=pq$.
steps: If p=h/2, then q=h²/p=2h. Their ratio is (h/2):(2h)=1:4.

problems.title: Perimeters after drawing a triangle midline
problems.question: Drawing midline MN splits a triangle into two figures whose perimeters differ by 6. Find MN.
problems.idea: Use the stated identity or geometric relation, preserving all domain and endpoint conditions.
formulas: The small triangle has half each original side length; subtract the two perimeters.
steps: If the original side lengths are a,b,c, with MN=c/2, the small perimeter is (a+b+c)/2. The trapezoid perimeter is (a+b)/2+3c/2.
The difference is c=6, so MN=c/2=3.

problems.title: Two nonnegative terms sum to zero
problems.question: How many roots has |x²−1|+|x+1|=0?
problems.idea: Use the stated identity or geometric relation, preserving all domain and endpoint conditions.
formulas: Both absolute values must individually be zero.
steps: The first allows x=±1; the second only x=−1. Their common solution is −1, giving one root.

problems.title: Exactly five integers in a half-open interval
problems.question: For which real k does x<2023,x≥k have exactly five integer solutions?
problems.idea: Use the stated identity or geometric relation, preserving all domain and endpoint conditions.
formulas: The largest integer is 2022; five integers require the least to be 2018.
steps: Thus ceil(k)=2018, equivalent to 2017<k≤2018. This includes exactly 2018,2019,2020,2021,2022.

problems.title: Opposite sign bounds force equality
problems.question: Solve |x|−x≤−x².
problems.idea: Use the stated identity or geometric relation, preserving all domain and endpoint conditions.
formulas: The left side is nonnegative and right side nonpositive.
steps: For the inequality to hold, both must be zero. The right side vanishes only at x=0, which satisfies the original inequality.

problems.title: Similar right triangles through a hypotenuse point
problems.question: ABC is right at C, K∈AB; KP⊥AC,KT⊥BC. AP=8,KP=10,KT=40. Find BT.
problems.idea: Use the stated identity or geometric relation, preserving all domain and endpoint conditions.
formulas: Use C=(0,0),A=(a,0),B=(0,b),K=(40,10); hypotenuse equation $x/a+y/b=1$.
steps: CP=KT=40, so AC=AP+CP=48. Substitute K: 40/48+10/b=1, giving b=60.

problems.title: A perpendicular from a hypotenuse
problems.question: ABE is right at B. D∈AE and DC⊥AE with C∈BE. DC=AB−2, DE=5,BE=8. Find AB.
problems.idea: Use the stated identity or geometric relation, preserving all domain and endpoint conditions.
formulas: Triangles CDE and ABE are similar: $CD/AB=DE/BE$.
steps: (AB−2)/AB=5/8. Thus 8AB−16=5AB, giving AB=16/3.

problems.title: Real square roots force a zero product
problems.question: Real quantities satisfy √(abc)=√(−a)√(−b)√(−c). Which listed condition must hold?
problems.idea: Use the stated identity or geometric relation, preserving all domain and endpoint conditions.
formulas: The right radicals require a,b,c≤0; the left requires abc≥0.
steps: Three nonpositive numbers have product at most zero. Combined with abc≥0 this forces abc=0.
This does not force all three to vanish: a=b=−1,c=0 is a counterexample to that stronger claim.

problems.title: Count positive-integer coordinate points
problems.question: Count points with positive integer coordinates satisfying y<−2x+6.
problems.idea: Use the stated identity or geometric relation, preserving all domain and endpoint conditions.
formulas: List the finitely many positive x with an allowed positive y.
steps: At x=1, y can be 1,2,3; at x=2, y can only be 1. For x≥3 the upper bound is nonpositive. Total=4.

problems.title: An intersection of integer solution sets
problems.question: Find the sum of integer x satisfying |x−4|≤3 and x²≤2|x|.
problems.idea: Use the stated identity or geometric relation, preserving all domain and endpoint conditions.
formulas: The first gives [1,7]; the second gives $|x|(|x|-2)\le0$, or [−2,2].
steps: The intersection is [1,2], whose integers 1 and 2 sum to 3.

problems.title: A diameter secant and a tangent
problems.question: A secant from external A passes through the nearest circle point. Its outside portion is one third its inside portion. A tangent from A has length 10. Find radius.
problems.idea: Use the stated identity or geometric relation, preserving all domain and endpoint conditions.
formulas: The secant passes through the centre, so its inside part is 2r; power of A gives tangent² = outside × whole.
steps: Let the outside part be t. The inside part is 3t, so 2r=3t. Then 100=t·4t, giving t=5 and r=7.5.

problems.title: A parallel through the centroid
problems.question: A,B medians meet at M. A line through M parallel to AB cuts the triangle internally. If AB=12, find its section length.
problems.idea: Use the stated identity or geometric relation, preserving all domain and endpoint conditions.
formulas: The centroid is one third of the altitude above the base, hence two thirds of the altitude from the opposite vertex.
steps: Similarity makes the parallel section 2/3 of AB. Its length is 12×2/3=8.

problems.title: A reciprocal sum without solving a quadratic
problems.question: Find m+1/m if (3m²−19m+3)/m=2.
problems.idea: Use the stated identity or geometric relation, preserving all domain and endpoint conditions.
formulas: Domain m≠0; divide the numerator term by term.

problems.title: A radical denominator and positivity
problems.question: Solve x/√(1−x)>0.
problems.idea: Use the stated identity or geometric relation, preserving all domain and endpoint conditions.
formulas: The denominator must be strictly positive, requiring x<1; then the fraction has the sign of x.
steps: Require x>0 as well, giving exactly 0<x<1. Both endpoints are excluded.

problems.title: A radical is an absolute value
problems.question: Count integer roots of √(x²−2x+1)≤3.
problems.idea: Use the stated identity or geometric relation, preserving all domain and endpoint conditions.
steps: The inequality gives −3≤x−1≤3, or −2≤x≤4. The seven integers in this interval are all valid.

problems.title: A point at one quarter of a trapezoid leg
problems.question: In right trapezoid ABCD, BC=1.2,AD=2 and slanted leg CD=20. K∈CD,CK=5. Find distance from K to vertical leg AB.
problems.idea: Use the stated identity or geometric relation, preserving all domain and endpoint conditions.
formulas: Horizontal distance from AB varies linearly along CD.
steps: K is CK/CD=1/4 of the way from C to D. Its horizontal distance is 1.2+(1/4)(2−1.2)=1.4.
Its perpendicular foot lies on segment AB, since K lies between the two base levels.

problems.title: Three tangent circles in an angle
problems.question: Three circles touch both sides of a 60° angle. The middle-radius circle touches both others. Find largest-radius/smallest-radius.
problems.idea: Use the stated identity or geometric relation, preserving all domain and endpoint conditions.
formulas: Centres lie at distance $2r$ from the angle vertex; external tangency of two requires $2(R-r)=R+r$.
steps: Thus each successive radius is three times the previous one. Across two steps the ratio is 3²=9.

problems.title: Two inequalities have the same full solution set
problems.question: How many positive k make √(x+2)≤k and |x|≤k equivalent?
problems.idea: Use the stated identity or geometric relation, preserving all domain and endpoint conditions.
formulas: For k>0 the sets are $[-2,k^2-2]$ and $[-k,k]$.
steps: Equality of the left endpoints forces k=2. Check the right endpoints: k²−2=2=k, so this value works. There is exactly one positive k.

problems.title: Count integers in a compound radical domain
problems.question: For how many integer x is [√(|x|−|x+3|)+√(x+13)]/|x+10| defined?
problems.idea: Use the stated identity or geometric relation, preserving all domain and endpoint conditions.
formulas: Require $|x|\ge|x+3|$, $x\ge-13$, $x\ne-10$.
steps: Squaring the first nonnegative comparison gives x²≥(x+3)², so x≤−3/2.
The integers from −13 to −2 total 12. Remove −10 for the zero denominator, leaving 11.

problems.title: Two nested radicals simplify using an order condition
problems.question: a,b,c>0 and a+b<c. Simplify √[a+b+c+2√(ac+bc)]+√[a+b+c−2√(ac+bc)].
problems.idea: Use the stated identity or geometric relation, preserving all domain and endpoint conditions.
formulas: Put u=a+b; $u+c\pm2\sqrt{uc}=(\sqrt u\pm\sqrt c)^2$.
steps: The sum is |√u+√c|+|√u−√c|. Since c>u>0, this is (√u+√c)+(√c−√u)=2√c.

problems.title: A tangent triangle from three arcs
problems.question: A radius-r circle is divided into arcs in ratio 3:4:5; their tangents form a triangle. From its middle-angle vertex C, a secant passes through the centre. Find its outside portion.
problems.idea: Use the stated identity or geometric relation, preserving all domain and endpoint conditions.
formulas: The arcs are 90°,120°,150°; each triangle angle is 180° minus the corresponding adjacent-contact arc.
steps: The triangle angles are 90°,60°,30°, so C=60°. Its incenter O lies on the bisector and has perpendicular distance r to the sides.
CO=r/sin30°=2r. The secant first reaches the circle r before O, so its outside portion is CO−r=r.

problems.title: Distance from a tangent point to a diameter
problems.question: Endpoints A,B of a diameter are distances 8,18 from a tangent line. Find the distance from its contact point T to line AB.
problems.idea: Use the stated identity or geometric relation, preserving all domain and endpoint conditions.
formulas: The midpoint O has tangent distance $R=(8+18)/2=13$.
steps: The component of the radius direction OA normal to the tangent has magnitude |18−8|/2=5. Thus the normal-to-tangent component of a unit direction along AB is 5/13.
The distance from T to line AB through O is R√(1−(5/13)²)=13×12/13=12. Equivalently it is √(8×18).
